description: Deterministic scripted assessment of the pinned httpx checkout. It demonstrates the pipeline end to end. It is not a model result and must never be cited as one.

events.text: Inspecting the package manifest and the public re-export surface.
Mapping the transport interface and the concrete transports.

messages.text: Read-only assessment written to the benchmark output directory.

output.summary: httpx is a published Python HTTP client library with a re-export facade, a client layer, a shared model surface and an explicit transport interface with four concrete transports. There is no ACIMA unit map, so the ACIMA rules cannot be measured yet; existing automation covers linting, typing and tests, not architectural dependency direction.

application.purpose: An HTTP client library consumed as an installed package

evidence.note: re-exports every public type and declares __all__
Request, Response and Headers imported package-wide

findings.rationale: Whether boundary operations separate validation from behaviour is a semantic judgement that needs recorded human evidence, not a scan result.
The concrete transport depends on the transport interface and httpcore; that dependency direction is the intended port/adapter seam rather than a boundary breach.

uncertainties: There is no ACIMA unit map yet; the module map above is a proposal that an owner must confirm.
The library profile is not implemented for Python in this ACIMA revision, so the published surface cannot be classified by the enforcer.
Whether the transport boundary is stable enough to freeze without waivers needs an owner decision.

proposedChanges.purpose: declare the reviewed units and roles
run the Python reference enforcer locally and in CI

uncertainties: This deterministic fixture demonstrates the output contract only; it does not perform semantic value-ownership analysis.
